title: Singapore's ScamShield flags about 5 million SMSes and blocks about 80,000 scam numbers by October 2023
summary: MHA told Parliament in November 2023 that ScamShield, built by Open Government Products with the NCPC and the Police, had about 750,000 downloads, about 80,000 numbers blacklisted and about 5 milli...
account: ScamShield is a Singapore government app developed by Open Government Products, a unit of GovTech, with the National Crime Prevention Council and the Singapore Police Force; GovInsider (June 2021) described an on-device machine-learning model that files suspected scam SMS into a junk folder and blocks calls from numbers on a police blocklist, reported 722,865 SMS messages reported and 5,537 numbers blocked since launch with a 95% detection accuracy claim, and quoted product manager Lennard Lim on the need for the model to adapt as scammers change their attacks. In an oral reply to parliamentary questions on 22 November 2023, Minister of State Sun Xueling said that ScamShield had about 750,000 downloads as of October 2023, that about 80,000 unique scam-tainted phone numbers had been blacklisted and blocked, that about 5 million SMSes had been flagged to users as potential scams, and that it has been effective in protecting users; she also cited about 180 million suspected scam calls blocked at network level in the first half of 2023, which is a telco measure separate from the app. No victim-level evaluation appears in the fetched sources; GovInsider's date comes from the RSS feed.
purpose: Filter scam SMS on-device and block calls from police-blacklisted numbers to protect users from scams.
developer: Open Government Products (GovTech) with the National Crime Prevention Council and the Singapore Police Force
deployer: Singapore Police Force and National Crime Prevention Council

ratings.reason: Flagged-SMS and blocked-number counts are aggregates; no loss avoided by an identifiable user is documented.
No measured change in scam losses is attributed to the app in the fetched sources.

ai_role.statement: GovInsider attributes SMS filtering to an on-device machine-learning model and call blocking to a police-maintained blocklist, so only the SMS figures involve the model; the parliamentary reply gives counts without attributing them to AI. Developer (Open Government Products, a public body) and deployer (the Police and NCPC) are both government bodies, and the reply was given by their ministry.
